data.body:
PLAN REVIEW NOW PASSES — certified, signed at b4b475b04, and SCOPED (this ticket now has
file_impact, so the attestation will no longer die stale-head on every commit the way the old
unscoped one did).

WHAT THE REMEDIATION CHANGED, from 7 blocking findings down to zero:

1. THE MECHANISM SECTION WAS FACTUALLY WRONG and was the root of 6 of the 7 findings. It claimed
   "resolution happens at the ONE funnel, config.resolve_model" while being labelled "decided on
   parent eb58 -- do not re-derive". The parent had ALREADY repudiated that: eb58 comment 4 says
   "My 'ONE funnel' keystone claim was WRONG", and the shipped code says it too --
   model_classes.py:238, "THERE IS NO SINGLE INTERCEPTION POINT". A leaf marked authoritative and
   off-limits was carrying a superseded decision. Rewritten to the corrected model: ONE FUNCTION
   (model_classes.resolve_model_string, which f844 ALREADY delivered and tested) wired at several
   call sites, with the lazy-import requirement for config.py spelled out because a module-level
   import there closes the very cycle model_classes' own docstring forbids.

2. A THIRD LADDER CONSUMER, previously in nobody's scope: workflow/runners.py:120,
   DefaultBatchRunner.run(), does `model = req.model_ladder[0] if req.model_ladder else None` --
   the identical split-brain to the two batch runners eb58 enumerated. Now in Scope with its own AC.

3. MODEL_LADDER's DUAL ROLE, which the plan would have silently broken. MEASURED at
   sizing.py:99-103 it is a table of (BARE_NAME, WINDOW_TOKENS) pairs driving BOTH escalation order
   (models_at_or_above, :312) AND P8's context budget (largest_window_tokens, :137-146, which
   matches with `if name in model` -- a SUBSTRING test). The old plan said the rungs "become CLASS
   names". That makes `"standard" in "bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6"` FALSE, so
   largest_window_tokens falls through to the ladder maximum for EVERY model and P8's budget changes
   with no error raised. DECISION RECORDED: keep MODEL_LADDER exactly as it is, keep
   largest_window_tokens byte-for-byte, and have models_at_or_above find the start rung with the
   existing substring match then map each at-or-above rung through the class config
   (haiku->trivial, sonnet->standard, opus->frontier). With no classes configured
   resolve_model_string returns names unchanged, so today's bare-id behaviour is preserved.

4. SCOPE was missing two files its own mechanism requires: config.py (resolve_model at :362) and
   plan_review/sizing.py (models_at_or_above at :312). Both added, with the existing couplings
   measured rather than assumed: a live monkeypatch of sizing.models_at_or_above at
   test_plan_review_prerequisites_model_log.py:43, the import-time alias at orchestrator.py:72 that
   two tests assert through, and test_resolve_model_precedence which pins the step > workflow >
   config ordering that class resolution must not disturb.

5. FOUR NEW ACs WITH REAL ORACLES: MODEL_LADDER unchanged plus a window-lookup regression test; a
   no-classes-configured back-compat control (which stops a "resolve always" implementation
   passing); coverage for runners.py:120; and an AST check that config.py has no module-level
   model_classes import.

READY TO CLAIM AND IMPLEMENT. Nothing is implemented yet -- no code touched for this ticket.
